+import unittest

+

+from appctl_cli.command import Command

+from appctl_cli.errors import SynopsisError

+from appctl_cli.synopsis import classify_token, parse_synopsis

+

+

+class ClassifyTokenTest(unittest.TestCase):

+    def test_positional(self):

+        token = classify_token("<site-name>")

+        self.assertEqual((token.type, token.name, token.optional), ("positional", "site-name", False))

+

+    def test_optional_repeating_positional(self):

+        token = classify_token("[<plugin>...]")

+        self.assertEqual((token.type, token.optional, token.repeating), ("positional", True, True))

+

+    def test_keyed_parameter(self):

+        token = classify_token("--type=<type>")

+        self.assertEqual((token.type, token.name, token.value_name), ("assoc", "type", "type"))

+

+    def test_flags(self):

+        self.assertEqual(classify_token("[--force]").type, "flag")

+        negatable = classify_token("[--[no-]color]")

+        self.assertEqual((negatable.type, negatable.name, negatable.negatable), ("flag", "color", True))

+

+    def test_mandatory_flag_is_malformed(self):

+        self.assertEqual(classify_token("--force").type, "unknown")

+

+    def test_generic(self):

+        self.assertEqual(classify_token("[--<field>=<value>]").type, "generic")

+

+    def test_malformed(self):

+        for token in ("site", "<bad name", "--type=type", "-f", "--[no-]x=<v>"):

+            self.assertEqual(classify_token(token).type, "unknown", token)

+

+    def test_parse(self):

+        types = [t.type for t in parse_synopsis("<a> [--b=<b>] [--c] [--<field>=<value>]")]

+        self.assertEqual(types, ["positional", "assoc", "flag", "generic"])

+

+    def test_malformed_synopsis_rejected_at_registration(self):

+        with self.assertRaises(SynopsisError):

+            Command("bad", synopsis="<ok> nonsense")

+

+

+if __name__ == "__main__":

+    unittest.main()

+"""Exception types used to signal user-facing failures."""

+

+

+class AppctlError(Exception):

+    """A fatal error reported as ``Error: <message>`` on STDERR."""

+

+    def __init__(self, message, exit_code=1):

+        super().__init__(message)

+        self.message = message

+        self.exit_code = exit_code

+

+

+class CommandNotFoundError(AppctlError):

+    """Raised when a command or subcommand cannot be resolved."""

+

+

+class UsageError(AppctlError):

+    """Raised when a command must print its usage on STDOUT and fail."""

+

+    def __init__(self, usage, exit_code=1):

+        super().__init__(usage, exit_code)

+        self.usage = usage

+

+

+class SynopsisError(ValueError):

+    """Raised when a command is registered with a malformed synopsis."""

+"""Global runtime configuration parameters."""

+

+from dataclasses import dataclass

+

+STRICT_ARGS_ENV = "APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"

+

+

+@dataclass(frozen=True)

+class GlobalParameter:

+    name: str

+    synopsis: str

+    description: str

+    default: object = None

+

+

+GLOBAL_PARAMETERS = {

+    p.name: p

+    for p in (

+        GlobalParameter("path", "--path=<path>", "Path to the application files.", None),

+        GlobalParameter("url", "--url=<url>", "Pretend request came from given URL.", None),

+        GlobalParameter("ssh", "--ssh=<[scheme:][user@]host|container>[:port][path]",

+                        "Perform operation against a remote server over SSH.", None),

+        GlobalParameter("http", "--http=<http>", "Perform operation against a remote install over HTTP.", None),

+        GlobalParameter("user", "--user=<id|login|email>", "Set the user for the current request.", None),

+        GlobalParameter("skip-plugins", "--skip-plugins[=<plugins>]", "Skip loading all or some plugins.", False),

+        GlobalParameter("skip-themes", "--skip-themes[=<themes>]", "Skip loading all or some themes.", False),

+        GlobalParameter("skip-packages", "--skip-packages", "Skip loading all installed packages.", False),

+        GlobalParameter("require", "--require=<path>", "Load a file before running the command.", None),

+        GlobalParameter("exec", "--exec=<php-code>", "Execute code before running the command.", None),

+        GlobalParameter("context", "--context=<context>", "Load the application in a given context.", "cli"),

+        GlobalParameter("color", "--[no-]color", "Whether to colorize the output.", "auto"),

+        GlobalParameter("debug", "--debug[=<group>]", "Show all errors and debug messages.", False),

+        GlobalParameter("prompt", "--prompt[=<assoc>]", "Prompt the user to enter values for all arguments.", False),

+        GlobalParameter("quiet", "--quiet", "Suppress informational messages.", False),

+    )

+}

+

+

+def is_global_parameter(key):

+    return key in GLOBAL_PARAMETERS

+

+

+def is_strict_mode(environ):

+    return bool(environ.get(STRICT_ARGS_ENV))

+

+

+def build_runtime_config(supplied):

+    """Merge supplied global values over the defaults."""

+    config = {name: param.default for name, param in GLOBAL_PARAMETERS.items()}

+    config.update(supplied)

+    return config

+"""Shared helpers for commands that list or display records."""

+

+from ..errors import AppctlError

+from ..formatter import format_item, format_items, format_value, select_fields

+

+RESERVED_KEYS = ("field", "fields", "format")

+

+LIST_OPTIONS = {

+    "field": "Prints the value of a single field for each item.",

+    "fields": "Limit the output to specific object fields.",

+    "format": "Render output in a particular format.",

+}

+

+

+def filter_items(items, assoc, available):

+    """Keep items matching every generic ``--<field>=<value>`` filter."""

+    filters = {k: v for k, v in assoc.items() if k not in RESERVED_KEYS and k in available}

+    return [

+        item for item in items

+        if all(str(item.get(k)) == str(v) for k, v in filters.items())

+    ]

+

+

+def render_list(ctx, items, assoc, default_fields, available=None, id_field="id"):

+    available = list(available or default_fields)

+    items = filter_items(items, assoc, available)

+    fmt = assoc.get("format", "table")

+    field = assoc.get("field")

+    if field and field is not True:

+        if field not in available:

+            raise AppctlError(f"Invalid field: {field}.")

+        values = [item.get(field) for item in items]

+        if fmt == "json":

+            ctx.output.line(format_value(values, "json"))

+        else:

+            for value in values:

+                ctx.output.line(format_value(value))

+        return

+    fields = select_fields(assoc.get("fields"), default_fields, available)

+    ctx.output.line(format_items(items, fields, fmt, id_field=id_field))

+

+

+def render_record(ctx, item, assoc, available):

+    field = assoc.get("field")

+    if field and field is not True:

+        if field not in available:

+            raise AppctlError(f"Invalid field: {field}.")

+        fmt = "json" if assoc.get("format") == "json" else "plaintext"

+        ctx.output.line(format_value(item.get(field), fmt))

+        return

+    fields = select_fields(assoc.get("fields"), available, available)

+    ctx.output.line(format_item(item, fields, assoc.get("format", "table")))

+

+

+def require_confirmation(assoc, question):

+    if not assoc.get("yes"):

+        raise AppctlError(f"{question} Re-run with --yes to confirm.")

+"""``appctl site``: site management (simulated)."""

+

+import re

+

+from ..errors import AppctlError

+from ._listing import LIST_OPTIONS, render_list, require_confirmation

+

+SITES = [

+    {"name": "blog", "type": "blog", "url": "https://blog.example.test", "status": "active"},

+    {"name": "main", "type": "standard", "url": "https://main.example.test", "status": "active"},

+    {"name": "shop", "type": "store", "url": "https://shop.example.test", "status": "archived"},

+]

+FIELDS = ["name", "type", "url", "status"]

+SITE_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$")

+

+

+def _find(name):

+    return next((s for s in SITES if s["name"] == name), None)

+

+

+def create(ctx, args, assoc):

+    name = args[0]

+    if not SITE_NAME_RE.match(name):

+        raise AppctlError(

+            f"Invalid site name '{name}'. Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only."

+        )

+    if _find(name):

+        raise AppctlError(f"Site '{name}' already exists.")

+    if assoc.get("porcelain"):

+        ctx.output.line(name)

+        return

+    title = assoc.get("title") or name

+    visibility = "private" if assoc.get("private") else "public"

+    ctx.output.success(

+        f"Site '{name}' created (type: {assoc['type']}, title: {title}, "

+        f"email: {assoc['email']}, visibility: {visibility})."

+    )

+

+

+def delete(ctx, args, assoc):

+    name = args[0]

+    if _find(name) is None:

+        raise AppctlError(f"Site '{name}' does not exist.")

+    require_confirmation(assoc, f"Are you sure you want to delete the '{name}' site?")

+    suffix = " Database tables were kept." if assoc.get("keep-tables") else ""

+    ctx.output.success(f"The site '{name}' was deleted.{suffix}")

+

+

+def list_(ctx, args, assoc):

+    render_list(ctx, SITES, assoc, FIELDS, id_field="name")

+

+

+def _set_status(status):

+    def handler(ctx, args, assoc):

+        failed = 0

+        for name in args:

+            site = _find(name)

+            if site is None:

+                ctx.output.warning(f"Site '{name}' does not exist.")

+                failed += 1

+            elif site["status"] == status:

+                ctx.output.warning(f"Site '{name}' is already {status}.")

+            else:

+                ctx.output.success(f"Site '{name}' {status}.")

+        return 1 if failed else 0

+    return handler

+

+

+def empty(ctx, args, assoc):

+    require_confirmation(assoc, "Are you sure you want to empty the site of all content?")

+    extra = " Uploaded files were removed." if assoc.get("uploads") else ""

+    ctx.output.success(f"The site was emptied.{extra}")

+

+

+def register(registry):

+    registry.add("site", description="Creates, deletes, empties, and lists sites.")

+    site_option = {"site-name": "The name of the site."}

+    registry.add(

+        "site activate", _set_status("active"),

+        synopsis="<site-name>...",

+        description="Activates one or more sites.",

+        options=site_option,

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "site archive", _set_status("archived"),

+        synopsis="<site-name>...",

+        description="Archives one or more sites.",

+        options=site_option,

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "site create", create,

+        synopsis="<site-name> [--type=<type>] [--title=<title>] [--email=<email>] "

+                 "[--[no-]private] [--porcelain]",

+        description="Creates a site.",

+        defaults={"type": "standard", "email": "admin@example.test", "private": False},

+        options=dict(site_option, type="The type of site to create.",

+                     title="Title of the new site. Defaults to the site name.",

+                     email="Email for the site admin.",

+                     private="If set, the new site will be non-public.",

+                     porcelain="If set, only the site name will be output on success."),

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "site delete", delete,

+        synopsis="<site-name> [--yes] [--keep-tables]",

+        description="Deletes a site.",

+        options=dict(site_option, yes="Answer yes to the confirmation message.",

+                     **{"keep-tables": "Delete the site but keep its database tables."}),

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "site empty", empty,

+        synopsis="[--uploads] [--yes]",

+        description="Empties a site of its content.",

+        options={"uploads": "Also delete uploaded files.",

+                 "yes": "Answer yes to the confirmation message."},

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "site list", list_,

+        synopsis="[--<field>=<value>] [--field=<field>] [--fields=<fields>] [--format=<format>]",

+        description="Lists all sites.",

+        alias="ls",

+        defaults={"format": "table"},

+        options=LIST_OPTIONS,

+    )

+"""``appctl cli``: information about appctl itself."""

+

+import json

+import platform

+

+from .. import PROGRAM_NAME, __version__

+from ..formatter import format_value

+from ..errors import AppctlError

+from ..resolver import try_resolve

+from ..runtime_config import GLOBAL_PARAMETERS

+

+

+def version(ctx, args, assoc):

+    ctx.output.line(f"{PROGRAM_NAME} {__version__}")

+

+

+def info(ctx, args, assoc):

+    data = {

+        "appctl_version": __version__,

+        "python_version": platform.python_version(),

+        "os": platform.system(),

+        "strict_args_mode": ctx.strict,

+        "runtime_config": {k: v for k, v in ctx.runtime.items()

+                           if v != GLOBAL_PARAMETERS[k].default},

+    }

+    if assoc["format"] == "json":

+        ctx.output.line(json.dumps(data))

+        return

+    if assoc["format"] != "list":

+        raise AppctlError(f"Invalid format: {assoc['format']}. Supported formats: list, json.")

+    ctx.output.line(f"appctl version:\t{data['appctl_version']}")

+    ctx.output.line(f"Python version:\t{data['python_version']}")

+    ctx.output.line(f"OS:\t{data['os']}")

+    ctx.output.line(f"Strict args mode:\t{'enabled' if ctx.strict else 'disabled'}")

+    for key, value in data["runtime_config"].items():

+        ctx.output.line(f"--{key}:\t{format_value(value)}")

+

+

+def param_dump(ctx, args, assoc):

+    dump = {}

+    for name, param in GLOBAL_PARAMETERS.items():

+        entry = {"synopsis": param.synopsis, "description": param.description,

+                 "default": param.default}

+        if assoc.get("with-values"):

+            entry["current"] = ctx.runtime.get(name)

+        dump[name] = entry

+    ctx.output.line(format_value(dump, "json"))

+

+

+def has_command(ctx, args, assoc):

+    tokens = " ".join(args).split()

+    resolved = try_resolve(ctx.root, tokens)

+    found = resolved is not None and not resolved[1]

+    return 0 if found else 1

+

+

+def register(registry):

+    registry.add("cli", description="Reviews current appctl info.")

+    registry.add("cli version", version, description="Prints the appctl version.")

+    registry.add(

+        "cli info", info,

+        synopsis="[--format=<format>]",

+        description="Prints various details about the appctl environment.",

+        defaults={"format": "list"},

+        options={"format": "Render output in a particular format (list, json)."},

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "cli param-dump", param_dump,

+        synopsis="[--with-values] [--format=<format>]",

+        description="Dumps the list of global parameters, as JSON.",

+        defaults={"format": "json"},

+        options={"with-values": "Display current values also."},

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "cli has-command", has_command,

+        synopsis="<command-name>...",

+        description="Detects if a command exists.",

+        options={"command-name": "The command to check."},

+    )

+"""``appctl option``: retrieve and set options (simulated)."""

+

+import fnmatch

+

+from ..errors import AppctlError

+from ..formatter import format_value

+from ._listing import LIST_OPTIONS, render_list

+

+OPTIONS = [

+    {"option_name": "admin_email", "option_value": "admin@example.test", "autoload": "yes"},

+    {"option_name": "blogname", "option_value": "My Application", "autoload": "yes"},

+    {"option_name": "home", "option_value": "https://example.test", "autoload": "yes"},

+    {"option_name": "siteurl", "option_value": "https://example.test", "autoload": "yes"},

+    {"option_name": "timezone_string", "option_value": "UTC", "autoload": "no"},

+]

+FIELDS = ["option_name", "option_value", "autoload"]

+

+

+def _find(key):

+    return next((o for o in OPTIONS if o["option_name"] == key), None)

+

+

+def add(ctx, args, assoc):

+    key, value = args

+    if _find(key):

+        raise AppctlError(f"Could not add option '{key}'. Does it already exist?")

+    ctx.output.success(f"Added '{key}' option (autoload: {assoc['autoload']}).")

+

+

+def delete(ctx, args, assoc):

+    for key in args:

+        if _find(key):

+            ctx.output.success(f"Deleted '{key}' option.")

+        else:

+            ctx.output.warning(f"Could not delete '{key}' option. Does it exist?")

+

+

+def get(ctx, args, assoc):

+    option = _find(args[0])

+    if option is None:

+        raise AppctlError(f"Could not get '{args[0]}' option. Does it exist?")

+    ctx.output.line(format_value(option["option_value"], assoc["format"]))

+

+

+def list_(ctx, args, assoc):

+    items = OPTIONS

+    pattern = assoc.get("search")

+    if pattern and pattern is not True:

+        items = [o for o in items if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(o["option_name"], pattern)]

+    autoload = assoc.get("autoload")

+    if autoload in ("on", "off", "yes", "no"):

+        wanted = "yes" if autoload in ("on", "yes") else "no"

+        items = [o for o in items if o["autoload"] == wanted]

+    filters = {k: v for k, v in assoc.items() if k not in ("search", "autoload")}

+    render_list(ctx, items, filters, ["option_name", "option_value"], FIELDS, id_field="option_name")

+

+

+def update(ctx, args, assoc):

+    key, value = args

+    option = _find(key)

+    if option and option["option_value"] == value:

+        ctx.output.success(f"Value passed for '{key}' option is unchanged.")

+    elif option:

+        ctx.output.success(f"Updated '{key}' option.")

+    else:

+        ctx.output.success(f"Added '{key}' option.")

+

+

+def register(registry):

+    registry.add("option", description="Retrieves and sets options, including plugin and theme settings.")

+    value_options = {

+        "key": "The name of the option.",

+        "value": "The value of the option.",

+        "format": "The serialization format for the value (plaintext, json).",

+        "autoload": "Should this option be automatically loaded (yes, no).",

+    }

+    registry.add(

+        "option add", add,

+        synopsis="<key> [<value>] [--format=<format>] [--autoload=<autoload>]",

+        description="Adds a new option value.",

+        defaults={"value": "", "format": "plaintext", "autoload": "yes"},

+        options=value_options,

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "option delete", delete,

+        synopsis="<key>...",

+        description="Deletes an option.",

+        options={"key": "Key for the option."},

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "option get", get,

+        synopsis="<key> [--format=<format>]",

+        description="Gets the value for an option.",

+        defaults={"format": "plaintext"},

+        options=value_options,

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        "option list", list_,

+        synopsis="[--search=<pattern>] [--autoload=<value>] [--field=<field>] "

+                 "[--fields=<fields>] [--format=<format>]",

+        description="Lists options and their values.",

+        defaults={"format": "table"},

+        options=dict(LIST_OPTIONS, search="Use wildcards ( * and ? ) to match option name.",

+                     autoload="Match only autoload options when value is on, and only "

+    )

+    registry.add(

+        description="Updates an option value.",

+"""End-to-end tests running appctl.py as a subprocess."""

+

+import os

+import re

+import subprocess

+import sys

+import unittest

+

+ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

+SCRIPT = os.path.join(ROOT, "appctl.py")

+

+

+def run(*args, strict=False):

+    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"}

+    if strict:

+        env["APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"] = "1"

+    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, SCRIPT, *args], capture_output=True, text=True,

+                          env=env, cwd=ROOT)

+

+

+class CliTest(unittest.TestCase):

+    def test_no_arguments_lists_commands_sorted_and_aligned(self):

+"""Argument rewrites applied before dispatch.

+

+* ``<command> --help`` becomes ``help <command>``.

+* ``--version`` (with no command) becomes ``cli version``.

+"""

+

+from .arguments import END_OF_OPTIONS, is_assoc_token, parse_assoc_token

+from .runtime_config import is_global_parameter

+

+

+def _split_options(argv):

+    """Return ``(head, tail)``; ``tail`` holds tokens after ``--``."""

+    if END_OF_OPTIONS in argv:

+        index = argv.index(END_OF_OPTIONS)

+        return argv[:index], argv[index + 1:]

+    return argv, []

+

+

+def rewrite_help(argv):

+    head, tail = _split_options(argv)

+    if "--help" not in head:

+        return argv

+    positional = [t for t in head if not is_assoc_token(t)] + tail

+    # Keep global parameters (ahead of 'help' so they stay global in strict

+    # mode); command-specific parameters are irrelevant to help output.

+    global_flags = [

+        t for t in head

+        if t != "--help" and is_assoc_token(t) and is_global_parameter(parse_assoc_token(t)[0])

+    ]

+    return global_flags + ["help"] + positional

+

+

+def rewrite_version(argv):

+    head, tail = _split_options(argv)

+    if "--version" not in head or tail or any(not is_assoc_token(t) for t in head):

+        return argv

+    rewritten = []

+    for token in head:

+        rewritten.extend(["cli", "version"] if token == "--version" else [token])

+    return rewritten

+

+

+def apply_rewrites(argv):

+    return rewrite_version(rewrite_help(list(argv)))

+"""Rendering of help text and usage lines."""

+

+from . import PROGRAM_NAME

+from .command import sort_key

+

+INDENT = "  "

+

+

+def command_line(command):

+    """``appctl <path> <synopsis>`` for a runnable command."""

+    parts = [PROGRAM_NAME] + command.path

+    if command.synopsis:

+        parts.append(command.synopsis)

+    return " ".join(parts)

+

+

+def composite_line(command):

+    return " ".join([PROGRAM_NAME] + command.path + ["<command>"])

+

+

+def usage_lines(command):

+    """All invocation forms of a command, sorted by full command path."""

+    lines = []

+    if command.is_runnable:

+        lines.append(command_line(command))

+    for sub in command.sorted_subcommands():

+        if sub.has_subcommands and not sub.is_runnable:

+            lines.append(composite_line(sub))

+        else:

+            lines.append(command_line(sub))

+    return lines

+

+

+def render_usage(command):

+    """The usage block printed when a command is invoked incorrectly."""

+    if not command.has_subcommands:

+        return f"usage: {command_line(command)}"

+    lines = usage_lines(command)

+    out = [f"usage: {lines[0]}"] + [f"   or: {line}" for line in lines[1:]]

+    out.append("")

+    out.append(

+        f"See '{PROGRAM_NAME} help {command.full_name} <command>' "

+        "for more information on a specific command."

+    )

+    return "\n".join(out)

+

+

+def render_listing(commands):

+    """Column-aligned ``name  description`` rows, alphabetically sorted."""

+    commands = sorted(commands, key=lambda c: sort_key(c.name))

+    if not commands:

+        return []

+    width = max(len(c.name) for c in commands)

+    return [f"{INDENT}{c.name.ljust(width)}  {c.description}".rstrip() for c in commands]

+

+

+def render_root_help(root):

+    lines = [

+        f"usage: {PROGRAM_NAME} <command> [<subcommand>] [<args>] [--<flags>]",

+        "",

+        "Available commands:",

+        "",

+    ]

+    lines.extend(render_listing(root.subcommands.values()))

+    lines.append("")

+    lines.append(

+        f"See '{PROGRAM_NAME} help <command>' for more information on a specific command."

+    )

+    return "\n".join(lines)

+

+

+def _section(title, body_lines):

+    return [title, ""] + body_lines + [""]

+

+

+def _default_text(value):

+    if isinstance(value, bool):

+        return "true" if value else "false"

+    return str(value)

+

+

+def _option_lines(command):

+    lines = []

+    for token in command.tokens:

+        lines.append(f"{INDENT}{token.token}")

+        description = command.options.get(token.name) if token.name else None

+        if description:

+            lines.append(f"{INDENT * 2}{description}")

+        if token.name and token.name in command.defaults:

+            lines.append(f"{INDENT * 2}---")

+            lines.append(f"{INDENT * 2}default: {_default_text(command.defaults[token.name])}")

+            lines.append(f"{INDENT * 2}---")

+        lines.append("")

+    return lines[:-1]

+

+

+def render_command_help(command):

+    if command.is_root:

+        return render_root_help(command)

+    lines = []

+    lines += _section("NAME", [f"{INDENT}{PROGRAM_NAME} {command.full_name}"])

+    if command.description:

+        lines += _section("DESCRIPTION", [f"{INDENT}{command.description}"])

+    if command.longdesc:

+        lines += [f"{INDENT}{line}".rstrip() for line in command.longdesc.splitlines()] + [""]

+    synopsis = []

+    if command.is_runnable:

+        synopsis.append(f"{INDENT}{command_line(command)}")

+    if command.has_subcommands:

+        synopsis.append(f"{INDENT}{composite_line(command)}")

+    lines += _section("SYNOPSIS", synopsis)

+    if command.is_runnable and command.tokens:

+        lines += _section("OPTIONS", _option_lines(command))

+    if command.has_subcommands:

+        lines += _section("SUBCOMMANDS", render_listing(command.subcommands.values()))

+    if command.alias:

+        lines += _section("ALIAS", [f"{INDENT}{command.alias}"])

+    return "\n".join(lines).rstrip("\n")

+    return next((p for p in POSTS if str(p["ID"]) == str(post_id)), None)

+    new_id = max(p["ID"] for p in POSTS) + 1

+    if assoc.get("porcelain"):

+        ctx.output.line(str(new_id))

+        return

+        else:

+            failed += 1

+"""Writers for the different kinds of user-facing output."""

+

+import sys

+

+

+class Output:

+    """Routes messages to STDOUT/STDERR, honouring --quiet and --debug."""

+

+    def __init__(self, quiet=False, debug=False, stdout=None, stderr=None):

+        self.quiet = quiet

+        self.debug_enabled = debug

+        self._stdout = stdout

+        self._stderr = stderr

+

+    @property

+    def stdout(self):

+        return self._stdout or sys.stdout

+

+    @property

+    def stderr(self):

+        return self._stderr or sys.stderr

+

+    def line(self, text=""):

+        """Print a line on STDOUT unconditionally."""

+        print(text, file=self.stdout)

+

+    def log(self, text):

+        """Print an informational line on STDOUT unless --quiet."""

+        if not self.quiet:

+            print(text, file=self.stdout)

+

+    def success(self, text):

+        if not self.quiet:

+            print(f"Success: {text}", file=self.stdout)

+

+    def warning(self, text):

+        if not self.quiet:

+            print(f"Warning: {text}", file=self.stderr)

+

+    def error(self, text):

+        print(f"Error: {text}", file=self.stderr)

+

+    def debug(self, text):

+        if self.debug_enabled:

+            print(f"Debug: {text}", file=self.stderr)

+"""Hierarchical resolution of positional tokens to a command."""

+

+from . import PROGRAM_NAME

+from .errors import CommandNotFoundError

+from .suggest import get_suggestion

+

+

+def _with_suggestion(message, typed, parent):

+    suggestion = get_suggestion(typed, parent.subcommand_names())

+    if suggestion:

+        message += f"\nDid you mean '{suggestion}'?"

+    return message

+

+

+def not_found_error(typed, parent):

+    if parent.is_root:

+        message = (

+            f"'{typed}' is not a registered {PROGRAM_NAME} command. "

+            f"See '{PROGRAM_NAME} help' for available commands."

+        )

+    else:

+        name = parent.full_name

+        message = (

+            f"'{typed}' is not a registered subcommand of '{name}'. "

+            f"See '{PROGRAM_NAME} help {name}' for available subcommands."

+        )

+    return CommandNotFoundError(_with_suggestion(message, typed, parent))

+

+

+def resolve(root, tokens):

+    """Walk the tree and return ``(command, remaining_tokens)``.

+

+    Tokens keep matching subcommands (by name or alias) until the deepest

+    command is found. If the next token does not match, a command with a

+    handler receives it as an argument; otherwise it is an error.

+    """

+    command = root

+    index = 0

+    while index < len(tokens) and command.has_subcommands:

+        child = command.find_subcommand(tokens[index])

+        if child is None:

+            if command.is_runnable and not command.is_root:

+                break

+            raise not_found_error(tokens[index], command)

+        command = child

+        index += 1

+    return command, list(tokens[index:])

+

+

+def try_resolve(root, tokens):

+    """Like :func:`resolve` but return ``None`` instead of raising."""

+    try:

+        return resolve(root, tokens)

+    except CommandNotFoundError:

+        return None

+"""Top-level orchestration: rewrite, parse, resolve, validate, run."""

+

+import os

+import sys

+

+from .arguments import parse_argv

+from .commands import build_command_tree

+from .context import Context

+from .errors import AppctlError, UsageError

+from .help import render_root_help, render_usage

+from .resolver import resolve

+from .rewrites import apply_rewrites

+from .runtime_config import build_runtime_config, is_strict_mode

+from .validator import ArgumentValidator

+from .output import Output

+

+

+def main(argv=None, environ=None, stdout=None, stderr=None):

+    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)

+    environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ

+    strict = is_strict_mode(environ)

+

+    parsed = parse_argv(apply_rewrites(argv), strict=strict)

+    runtime = build_runtime_config(parsed.runtime)

+    output = Output(quiet=bool(runtime["quiet"]), debug=bool(runtime["debug"]),

+                    stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr)

+    root = build_command_tree()

+

+    try:

+        if not parsed.positional:

+            output.line(render_root_help(root))

+            return 0

+        command, remaining = resolve(root, parsed.positional)

+        if not command.is_runnable:

+            output.line(render_usage(command))

+            return 0

+        output.debug(f"Running command: {command.full_name}")

+        args, assoc = ArgumentValidator(command).validate(

+            remaining, parsed.assoc, warn=output.warning

+        )

+        context = Context(root=root, command=command, output=output,

+                          runtime=runtime, strict=strict)

+        result = command.handler(context, args, assoc)

+        return int(result or 0)

+    except UsageError as exc:

+        output.line(exc.usage)

+        return exc.exit_code

+    except AppctlError as exc:

+        output.error(exc.message)

+        return exc.exit_code

+

+import os

+from ._listing import LIST_OPTIONS, render_list

+

+CONFIG_FILE = "config.php"

+

+    {"name": "DB_NAME", "value": "appctl", "type": "constant"},

+    {"name": "DB_USER", "value": "appctl", "type": "constant"},

+    {"name": "DB_HOST", "value": "localhost", "type": "constant"},

+    {"name": "DEBUG", "value": False, "type": "constant"},

+    {"name": "table_prefix", "value": "app_", "type": "variable"},

+]

+

+def _check_type(entry_type):

+    if entry_type not in TYPES:

+        raise AppctlError(f"Invalid type '{entry_type}'. Expected one of: {', '.join(TYPES)}.")

+

+

+def _find(name, entry_type):

+    _check_type(entry_type)

+    for entry in ENTRIES:

+        if entry["name"] == name and entry_type in ("all", entry["type"]):

+            return entry

+    return None

+

+

+def _label(entry_type):

+    return "constant or variable" if entry_type == "all" else entry_type

+    verb = "Updated" if entry else "Added"

+    preposition = "in" if entry else "to"

+    raw = " (raw)" if assoc.get("raw") else ""

+        f"{verb} the {kind} '{name}' {preposition} the '{CONFIG_FILE}' file with the{raw} value '{value}'."

+    )

+

+"""Parsing and classification of command synopsis strings."""

+

+import re

+from dataclasses import dataclass

+from typing import Optional

+

+POSITIONAL = "positional"

+ASSOC = "assoc"

+FLAG = "flag"

+GENERIC = "generic"

+UNKNOWN = "unknown"

+

+GENERIC_TOKEN = "--<field>=<value>"

+

+_NAME = r"[a-z0-9_-]+"

+_VALUE = r"[a-zA-Z0-9_|,-]+"

+_POSITIONAL_RE = re.compile(rf"^<({_VALUE})>$")

+_PARAM_RE = re.compile(rf"^--(\[no-\])?({_NAME})")

+_VALUE_RE = re.compile(rf"^=<({_VALUE})>$")

+

+

+@dataclass(frozen=True)

+class SynopsisToken:

+    """One classified token of a synopsis string."""

+

+    token: str

+    type: str

+    name: Optional[str] = None

+    optional: bool = False

+    repeating: bool = False

+    value_name: Optional[str] = None

+    value_optional: bool = False

+    negatable: bool = False

+

+    @property

+    def is_positional(self):

+        return self.type == POSITIONAL

+

+    @property

+    def is_parameter(self):

+        """True for named ``--key=<value>`` and ``--flag`` tokens."""

+        return self.type in (ASSOC, FLAG)

+

+

+def _strip_optional(text):

+    if len(text) >= 2 and text.startswith("[") and text.endswith("]"):

+        return True, text[1:-1]

+    return False, text

+

+

+def _strip_repeating(text):

+    if text.endswith("..."):

+        return True, text[:-3]

+    return False, text

+

+

+def classify_token(token):

+    """Classify a single synopsis token."""

+    optional, body = _strip_optional(token)

+    repeating, body = _strip_repeating(body)

+    unknown = SynopsisToken(token=token, type=UNKNOWN)

+

+    if body == GENERIC_TOKEN:

+        return SynopsisToken(token, GENERIC, optional=optional, repeating=repeating)

+

+    match = _POSITIONAL_RE.match(body)

+    if match:

+        return SynopsisToken(token, POSITIONAL, name=match.group(1),

+                             optional=optional, repeating=repeating)

+

+    match = _PARAM_RE.match(body)

+    if not match:

+        return unknown

+    negatable = bool(match.group(1))

+    name = match.group(2)

+    rest = body[match.end():]

+

+    if rest == "":

+        # Boolean flags are by nature optional.

+        if not optional:

+            return unknown

+        return SynopsisToken(token, FLAG, name=name, optional=True,

+                             repeating=repeating, negatable=negatable)

+

+    if negatable:

+        return unknown

+    value_optional, rest = _strip_optional(rest)

+    value_match = _VALUE_RE.match(rest)

+    if not value_match:

+        return unknown

+    return SynopsisToken(token, ASSOC, name=name, optional=optional,

+                         repeating=repeating, value_name=value_match.group(1),

+                         value_optional=value_optional)

+

+

+def parse_synopsis(synopsis):

+    """Split a synopsis string into classified tokens."""

+    return [classify_token(token) for token in (synopsis or "").split()]

+

+

+def invalid_tokens(tokens):

+    """Return the raw text of every malformed token."""

+    return [t.token for t in tokens if t.type == UNKNOWN]

+

+from ..errors import AppctlError

+from ._listing import render_list

+

+LIST_FIELDS = ["name", "status", "update", "version"]

+

+

+class ExtensionCatalog:

+    """A simulated collection of installed plugins or themes."""

+

+    def __init__(self, noun, items):

+        self.noun = noun

+        self.items = items

+

+    def find(self, name):

+        return next((i for i in self.items if i["name"] == name), None)

+

+    def targets(self, args, assoc):

+        """Resolve the named items, or every item with ``--all``."""

+        if assoc.get("all"):

+            return [i["name"] for i in self.items]

+        if not args:

+            raise AppctlError(f"Please specify one or more {self.noun}s, or use --all.")

+        return list(args)

+

+    def each_installed(self, ctx, names):

+        for name in names:

+            if self.find(name) is None:

+                ctx.output.warning(f"The '{name}' {self.noun} could not be found.")

+            else:

+                yield name

+

+    # -- handlers -------------------------------------------------------

+

+    def list(self, ctx, args, assoc):

+        render_list(ctx, self.items, assoc, LIST_FIELDS, LIST_FIELDS + ["title"], id_field="name")

+

+    def status(self, ctx, args, assoc):

+        if args:

+            item = self.find(args[0])

+            if item is None:

+                raise AppctlError(f"The '{args[0]}' {self.noun} could not be found.")

+            ctx.output.line(f"{self.noun.capitalize()} {item['name']} details:")

+            ctx.output.line(f"    Name: {item['title']}")

+            ctx.output.line(f"    Status: {item['status'].capitalize()}")

+            ctx.output.line(f"    Version: {item['version']}")

+            return

+        ctx.output.line(f"{len(self.items)} installed {self.noun}s:")

+        for item in self.items:

+            marker = "A" if item["status"] == "active" else "I"

+            ctx.output.line(f"  {marker} {item['name']} {item['version']}")

+

+    def install(self, ctx, args, assoc):

+        for name in args:

+            if self.find(name) and not assoc.get("force"):

+                ctx.output.warning(f"{name}: {self.noun.capitalize()} already installed.")

+                continue

+            ctx.output.log(f"Installing {name} ({assoc['version']})...")

+            if assoc.get("activate"):

+                ctx.output.log(f"Activating '{name}'...")

+        ctx.output.success(f"Installed {len(args)} of {len(args)} {self.noun}s.")

+

+    def delete(self, ctx, args, assoc):

+        names = self.targets(args, assoc)

+        deleted = list(self.each_installed(ctx, names))

+        for name in deleted:

+            ctx.output.log(f"Deleted '{name}' {self.noun}.")

+        self.summary(ctx, "Deleted", len(deleted), len(names))

+

+    def update(self, ctx, args, assoc):

+        names = self.targets(args, assoc)

+        found = list(self.each_installed(ctx, names))

+        if assoc.get("dry-run"):

+            ctx.output.log(f"Available {self.noun} updates: {', '.join(found) or 'none'}")

+            return

+        self.summary(ctx, "Updated", len(found), len(names))

+

+    def summary(self, ctx, verb, done, total):

+        if done == total:

+            ctx.output.success(f"{verb} {done} of {total} {self.noun}s.")

+        else:

+            raise AppctlError(f"Only {verb.lower()} {done} of {total} {self.noun}s.")

+    """A node in the command tree.

+

+    A command may have a handler, subcommands, or both. A command with

+    subcommands but no handler only prints its usage when invoked.

+    """

+

+    def __init__(self, name, description="", synopsis="", handler=None,

+                 alias=None, defaults=None, options=None, longdesc=""):

+        self.name = name

+        self.description = description

+        self.synopsis = " ".join((synopsis or "").split())

+        self.handler = handler

+        self.alias = alias

+        self.defaults = dict(defaults or {})

+        self.options = dict(options or {})

+        self.longdesc = longdesc

+        self.parent = None

+        self.subcommands = {}

+

+        self.tokens = parse_synopsis(self.synopsis)

+        bad = invalid_tokens(self.tokens)

+        if bad:

+            raise SynopsisError(

+                f"The '{name}' command has an invalid synopsis part: {', '.join(bad)}"

+            )

+

+    # -- tree structure -------------------------------------------------

+

+    def add_subcommand(self, command):

+        for taken in self._taken_names():

+            if taken in (command.name, command.alias):

+                raise ValueError(

+                    f"'{taken}' is already registered under '{self.full_name or 'appctl'}'"

+                )

+        command.parent = self

+        self.subcommands[command.name] = command

+        return command

+

+    def _taken_names(self):

+        for sub in self.subcommands.values():

+            yield sub.name

+            if sub.alias:

+                yield sub.alias

+

+    def find_subcommand(self, token):

+        """Match a subcommand by canonical name first, then by alias."""

+        if token in self.subcommands:

+            return self.subcommands[token]

+        for sub in self.subcommands.values():

+            if sub.alias and sub.alias == token:

+                return sub

+        return None

+

+    def sorted_subcommands(self):

+        return [self.subcommands[k] for k in sorted(self.subcommands, key=sort_key)]

+

+    def subcommand_names(self):

+        return list(self.subcommands)

+

+    # -- properties -----------------------------------------------------

+

+    @property

+    def is_root(self):

+        return self.parent is None

+

+    @property

+    def has_subcommands(self):

+        return bool(self.subcommands)

+

+    @property

+    def is_runnable(self):

+        return self.handler is not None

+

+    @property

+    def path(self):

+        """Canonical names from the top-level command down to this one."""

+        parts = []

+        node = self

+        while node is not None and not node.is_root:

+            parts.append(node.name)

+            node = node.parent

+        return list(reversed(parts))

+

+    @property

+    def full_name(self):

+        return " ".join(self.path)

+

+    def tokens_of_type(self, *types):

+        return [t for t in self.tokens if t.type in types]

+

+    def __repr__(self):

+        return f"Command({self.full_name or '<root>'!r})"

+"""Deterministic "Did you mean?" suggestions."""

+

+DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 2

+

+# Curated synonyms for common command-name variants. A synonym is only

+# suggested when its target is one of the registered options.

+SYNONYMS = {

+    "add": "create",

+    "check": "check-update",

+    "capability": "cap",

+    "clear": "flush",

+    "decrement": "decr",

+    "del": "delete",

+    "directory": "dir",

+    "exec": "eval",

+    "exec-file": "eval-file",

+    "increment": "incr",

+    "language": "locale",

+    "lang": "locale",

+    "new": "create",

+    "number": "count",

+    "remove": "delete",

+    "regen": "regenerate",

+    "rep": "replace",

+    "repl": "replace",

+    "rm": "delete",

+    "trash": "delete",

+    "v": "version",

+}

+

+

+def levenshtein(source, target):

+    """Return the edit distance between two strings."""

+    if source == target:

+        return 0

+    if not source:

+        return len(target)

+    if not target:

+        return len(source)

+    previous = list(range(len(target) + 1))

+    for i, s_char in enumerate(source, start=1):

+        current = [i]

+        for j, t_char in enumerate(target, start=1):

+            current.append(min(

+                previous[j] + 1,

+                current[j - 1] + 1,

+                previous[j - 1] + (s_char != t_char),

+            ))

+        previous = current

+    return previous[-1]

+

+

+def get_suggestion(target, options, threshold=DEFAULT_THRESHOLD):

+    """Return the closest option to ``target`` or ``None``.

+

+    Synonyms win over edit distance. A match must be within ``threshold``

+    edits and must not replace every character of ``target``. Ties are

+    broken alphabetically (case-insensitively) so the result is stable.

+    """

+    candidates = sorted(set(options), key=lambda o: (o.lower(), o))

+    if not candidates:

+        return None

+

+    synonym = SYNONYMS.get(target)

+    if synonym is not None and synonym in candidates:

+        return synonym

+

+    best_distance, best = None, None

+    for option in candidates:

+        distance = levenshtein(target, option)

+        if best_distance is None or distance < best_distance:

+            best_distance, best = distance, option

+

+    if best_distance <= threshold and best_distance < len(target) and best != target:

+        return best

+    return None

+"""Rendering of records as table, csv, json, yaml, count or ids."""

+

+import csv

+import io

+import json

+

+from .errors import AppctlError

+

+LIST_FORMATS = ("table", "csv", "json", "yaml", "count", "ids")

+ITEM_FORMATS = ("table", "csv", "json", "yaml")

+

+

+def _text(value):

+    if value is None:

+        return ""

+    if isinstance(value, bool):

+        return "true" if value else "false"

+    return str(value)

+

+

+def _check_format(fmt, allowed):

+    if fmt not in allowed:

+        raise AppctlError(f"Invalid format: {fmt}. Supported formats: {', '.join(allowed)}.")

+

+

+def select_fields(requested, default_fields, available):

+    """Resolve ``--fields`` (comma separated) against the known fields."""

+    if not requested or requested is True:

+        return list(default_fields)

+    fields = [f.strip() for f in str(requested).split(",") if f.strip()]

+    for name in fields:

+        if name not in available:

+            raise AppctlError(f"Invalid field: {name}.")

+    return fields

+

+

+def _table(headers, rows):

+    widths = [len(h) for h in headers]

+    for row in rows:

+        widths = [max(w, len(cell)) for w, cell in zip(widths, row)]

+    border = "+" + "+".join("-" * (w + 2) for w in widths) + "+"

+

+    def render(cells):

+        return "|" + "|".join(f" {c.ljust(w)} " for c, w in zip(cells, widths)) + "|"

+

+    lines = [border, render(headers), border]

+    lines += [render(row) for row in rows]

+    lines.append(border)

+    return "\n".join(lines)

+

+

+def _csv(headers, rows):

+    buffer = io.StringIO()

+    writer = csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator="\n")

+    writer.writerow(headers)

+    writer.writerows(rows)

+    return buffer.getvalue().rstrip("\n")

+

+

+def _yaml_scalar(value):

+    text = _text(value)

+    if text == "" or any(ch in text for ch in ":#'\"{}[],&*!|>%@`") or text.strip() != text:

+        return json.dumps(text)

+    return text

+

+

+def format_items(items, fields, fmt="table", id_field="id"):

+    _check_format(fmt, LIST_FORMATS)

+    if fmt == "count":

+        return str(len(items))

+    if fmt == "ids":

+        return " ".join(_text(item.get(id_field)) for item in items)

+    if fmt == "json":

+        return json.dumps([{f: item.get(f) for f in fields} for item in items])

+    if fmt == "yaml":

+        if not items:

+            return "--- []"

+        lines = ["---"]

+        for item in items:

+            for index, name in enumerate(fields):

+                prefix = "- " if index == 0 else "  "

+                lines.append(f"{prefix}{name}: {_yaml_scalar(item.get(name))}")

+        return "\n".join(lines)

+    rows = [[_text(item.get(f)) for f in fields] for item in items]

+    if fmt == "csv":

+        return _csv(fields, rows)

+    return _table(fields, rows)

+

+

+def format_item(item, fields, fmt="table"):

+    _check_format(fmt, ITEM_FORMATS)

+    if fmt == "json":

+        return json.dumps({f: item.get(f) for f in fields})

+    if fmt == "yaml":

+        return "\n".join(["---"] + [f"{f}: {_yaml_scalar(item.get(f))}" for f in fields])

+    rows = [[f, _text(item.get(f))] for f in fields]

+    if fmt == "csv":

+        return _csv(["Field", "Value"], rows)

+    return _table(["Field", "Value"], rows)

+

+

+def format_value(value, fmt="plaintext"):

+    if fmt == "json":

+        return json.dumps(value)

+    if fmt == "plaintext":

+        return _text(value)

+    raise AppctlError(f"Invalid format: {fmt}. Supported formats: plaintext, json.")

+"""Registration of commands into a tree rooted at the program command."""

+

+from . import PROGRAM_NAME

+from .command import Command

+

+

+class CommandRegistry:

+    """Builds the command tree from multi-level command paths."""

+

+    def __init__(self, description=""):

+        self.root = Command(PROGRAM_NAME, description=description)

+

+    def add(self, path, handler=None, **attributes):

+        """Register ``path`` (e.g. ``"site create"``) and return the command.

+

+        Parent commands must be registered before their subcommands.

+        """

+        parts = path.split()

+        if not parts:

+            raise ValueError("A command path cannot be empty")

+        parent = self.root

+        for index, part in enumerate(parts[:-1]):

+            child = parent.subcommands.get(part)

+            if child is None:

+                missing = " ".join(parts[: index + 1])

+                raise ValueError(f"Parent command '{missing}' must be registered before '{path}'")

+            parent = child

+        return parent.add_subcommand(Command(parts[-1], handler=handler, **attributes))

+

+    def get(self, path):

+        node = self.root

+        for part in path.split():

+            node = node.subcommands[part]

+        return node

+"""Validation of supplied arguments against a command's synopsis."""

+

+from .errors import AppctlError, UsageError

+from .help import render_usage

+from .suggest import get_suggestion

+from .synopsis import ASSOC, FLAG, GENERIC, POSITIONAL

+

+

+class ArgumentValidator:

+    """Checks positional and associative arguments for one command."""

+

+    def __init__(self, command):

+        self.command = command

+        self.positionals = command.tokens_of_type(POSITIONAL)

+        self.parameters = command.tokens_of_type(ASSOC, FLAG)

+        self.accepts_any_assoc = bool(command.tokens_of_type(GENERIC))

+

+    # -- positional -----------------------------------------------------

+

+    def enough_positionals(self, args):

+        required = sum(1 for t in self.positionals if not t.optional)

+        return len(args) >= required

+

+    def unknown_positionals(self, args):

+        if any(t.repeating for t in self.positionals):

+            return []

+        return list(args[len(self.positionals):])

+

+    # -- associative ----------------------------------------------------

+

+    def assoc_errors(self, assoc, warn):

+        """Return fatal errors; drop optional keyed params given no value."""

+        errors = []

+        for param in self.parameters:

+            key = param.name

+            if param.type != ASSOC:

+                continue

+            value = assoc.get(key)

+            if not param.optional:

+                if value is None or value is True or value is False or value == "":

+                    errors.append(f"missing --{key} parameter")

+            elif value is True and not param.value_optional:

+                warn(f"--{key} parameter needs a value")

+                del assoc[key]

+        for key in self.unknown_assoc(assoc):

+            message = f"unknown --{key} parameter"

+            suggestion = get_suggestion(key, [p.name for p in self.parameters])

+            if suggestion:

+                message += f"\nDid you mean '--{suggestion}'?"

+            errors.append(message)

+        return errors

+

+    def unknown_assoc(self, assoc):

+        if self.accepts_any_assoc:

+            return []

+        known = {p.name for p in self.parameters}

+        return [key for key in assoc if key not in known]

+

+    # -- defaults -------------------------------------------------------

+

+    def apply_defaults(self, args, assoc):

+        defaults = self.command.defaults

+        for index, token in enumerate(self.positionals):

+            if index < len(args):

+                continue

+            if token.name in defaults and len(args) == index:

+                args.append(defaults[token.name])

+            else:

+                break

+        for param in self.parameters:

+            if param.name not in assoc and param.name in defaults:

+                assoc[param.name] = defaults[param.name]

+

+    # -- entry point ----------------------------------------------------

+

+    def validate(self, args, assoc, warn=lambda message: None):

+        """Validate and return ``(args, assoc)`` with defaults applied."""

+        args = list(args)

+        assoc = dict(assoc)

+        if not self.enough_positionals(args):

+            raise UsageError(render_usage(self.command))

+        extra = self.unknown_positionals(args)

+        if extra:

+            raise AppctlError("Too many positional arguments: " + " ".join(extra))

+        errors = self.assoc_errors(assoc, warn)

+        if errors:

+            raise AppctlError("Parameter errors:\n" + "\n".join(f" {e}" for e in errors))

+        self.apply_defaults(args, assoc)

+        return args, assoc

+"""Splitting raw argv into positional, associative and global arguments."""

+

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field

+

+from .runtime_config import is_global_parameter

+

+END_OF_OPTIONS = "--"

+

+

+def is_assoc_token(token):

+    """True for ``--key``, ``--key=value`` and ``--no-key`` tokens."""

+    return token.startswith("--") and len(token) > 2

+

+

+def parse_assoc_token(token):

+    """Return ``(key, value)`` for an associative token.

+

+    ``--key=value`` yields the string value, ``--no-key`` yields ``False``

+    and a bare ``--key`` yields ``True``.

+    """

+    body = token[2:]

+    if "=" in body:

+        key, value = body.split("=", 1)

+        return key, value

+    if body.startswith("no-"):

+        return body[3:], False

+    return body, True

+

+

+@dataclass

+class ParsedArguments:

+    positional: list = field(default_factory=list)

+    assoc: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

+    runtime: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

+

+

+def parse_argv(argv, strict=False):

+    """Classify every argv token.

+

+    Global parameters become runtime configuration. In strict mode only

+    those appearing before the first positional token are treated as

+    global; afterwards every argument is command-specific.

+    """

+    parsed = ParsedArguments()

+    end_of_options = False

+    seen_positional = False

+    for token in argv:

+        if not end_of_options and token == END_OF_OPTIONS:

+            end_of_options = True

+            continue

+        if end_of_options or not is_assoc_token(token):

+            parsed.positional.append(token)

+            seen_positional = True

+            continue

+        key, value = parse_assoc_token(token)

+        if is_global_parameter(key) and not (strict and seen_positional):

+            parsed.runtime[key] = value

+        else:

+            parsed.assoc[key] = value

+    return parsed
